reason: The text explicitly depicts Yahweh as bound to and identified with the nation of Israel. Multiple passages establish this: Yahweh claims the Israelites as 'my people' (עַמִּי) and is moved by their national affliction in Egypt. God identifies Himself as 'the God of the Hebrews' (אֱלֹהֵי הָעִבְרִיִּים) and 'the God of your fathers' (אֱלֹהֵי אֲבֹתֵיכֶם), connecting Him to the patriarchal covenant and national identity. Crucially, Yahweh promises to liberate this specific people from Egypt and bring them to a land promised to their nation, commissioning Moses specifically for their national deliverance. The entire passage frames Yahweh's intervention as directed toward establishing and liberating a particular people, demonstrating His role as a national deity bound to Israel's fortunes.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
